CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Controls are decision days in the bottom three SWEEP_COUNT_24H quintiles, matched 1:1 on YEAR x trailing RV_24H decile x weekday and compared within those strata. The null distribution comes from permuting the SWEEP_COUNT_24H quintile label within YEAR x RV decile strata. A second null is a GARCH(1,1)-t surrogate fitted on 1m log returns, with a simulated high-low envelope from the empirical range-to-return ratio. It produces both SWEEP_COUNT_24H and TAIL_EXC_24H from one volatility-clustering model, which tests whether the association is implied by volatility dynamics alone.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Exchange liquidation engines and clustered stop orders send market orders that ignore price. When near-touch depth is thin, such an order walks several levels inside one minute and price then reclaims as makers refill the book. This leaves a long wick with a close back near the bar open. Each sweep imposes adverse selection on resting liquidity providers. They respond for hours by quoting less size, for inventory and toxicity reasons. The leveraged positioning that produced the sweep is usually only partly flushed. A high count of sweep-and-reclaim bars over a day therefore marks a fragile book: later shocks of ordinary size should travel further before meeting resting liquidity. RV cannot separate this fragility from informative trending moves, because RV is high in both cases. The reclaim geometry isolates the non-informative, forced-flow part. As an abstention mechanism, a decision process would stand aside from new exposure when this fragility footprint is elevated.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT perpetual 1m open, high, low and close used for wick geometry, trailing range medians, RV_24H and close-path excursions

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It separates forced-flow book fragility from volatility level using only ready data, and its outcome decides whether liquidation footprints justify costly order-book follow-up.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The fragility mechanism is rejected for this observable in either of two cases. First, the mean TAIL_EXC_24H on top-quintile SWEEP_COUNT_24H days minus matched controls is at or below the 95th percentile of the within-stratum permutation null. Second, the GARCH surrogate reproduces a gap of comparable size, within its own 5-95 percentile band.

CARD.MECHANISM: Sweep-and-reclaim 1m wicks are footprints of forced liquidation and stop flow hitting a thin book. Such a book state lasts for hours and raises the unsigned tail excursion of the next 24h beyond what RV implies.

For an upper wick the retrace is (high-close)/(high-low); for a lower wick it is (close-low)/(high-low).

A sign-flip null randomizes sign(Z_D) within week x hour blocks. A block-bootstrap null resamples joint perp and spot 5m returns within weekends in 1-hour blocks; it keeps contemporaneous co-movement, destroys signed premium-to-spot lead structure, and produces the full ALIGNED_SPOT_RET_H statistic.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: On weekdays, cross-venue relative-value desks with fiat and collateral access close Binance-perp versus OKX-spot gaps by taking offsetting positions on both legs, so neither leg drifts in a predictable direction. On weekends bank transfer rails are closed and many institutional desks run reduced books and reduced collateral mobility. Leveraged perpetual participants then dominate incremental price formation, while OKX spot makers update quotes toward the perp with a lag. If a weekend perp premium reflects real directional demand from leveraged participants, not noise, the spot leg should drift in the premium's direction over the next minutes to hours. The constraint is the weekend immobility of balance-sheet capital that would otherwise neutralize the gap.

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It tests a specific institutional-calendar channel for directional information in the cross-venue premium, which no prior card measured on the spot leg.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The weekend propagation claim is rejected in either of two cases. First, the mean ALIGNED_SPOT_RET_H over weekend events minus the matched within-regime control mean does not exceed the 95th percentile of the sign-flip null. Second, the statistic is negative, meaning the perp reverts toward spot rather than spot following the perp.
CARD.FUNCTION: Regime fixed in advance: WEEKEND, meaning decision times T from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Sunday 23:55 UTC. Within this regime only, measure the mean OKX spot log return over (T, T+H] signed by sign(Z_D(T)), for events with |Z_D(T)| at least z. Weekday events are neither pooled nor used to choose z or H.
CARD.HORIZON: H in {30 minutes, 2 hours} after each weekend 5m event close T, with events de-clustered to a minimum 2-hour spacing
CARD.MECHANISM: While fiat rails and institutional desks are inactive on weekends, a Binance perp premium over OKX spot carries the directional demand of leveraged participants, and spot drifts toward the perp rather than the perp reverting.
CARD.NAME: Weekend perp-premium propagation into OKX spot
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Z_D(T): the aligned 5m-close log(perp/OKX spot) at T minus its trailing 7-day median, divided by its trailing 7-day median absolute deviation
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: ALIGNED_SPOT_RET_H: sign(Z_D(T)) x log(OKX spot close at T+H / OKX spot close at T), averaged over de-clustered weekend events with |Z_D(T)| at least z, minus the matched within-regime control mean

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: The main-effect baseline regresses log(1+RUN_LEN) on Down-move direction of the triggering 5m jump, on Inverse-collateral contract structure of BitMEX XBTUSD versus USDT-margined Binance perpetual, and on daily-RV-bin fixed effects within each contract. The claim is only the coefficient on the product of the two components, beyond both main effects. For the null, within each contract every UTC day's 5m return path is multiplied by an independent random sign. This keeps intraday clustering, magnitudes and run structure, but equalizes down and up dynamics within each contract. The surrogate produces RUN_LEN and the full interaction statistic, so its distribution is centered on no direction-specific contract effect.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: On the inverse XBTUSD contract, margin and PnL are in BTC while the contract is denominated in USD. The BTC loss of a leveraged long is N(1/P - 1/P0), which grows convexly as price falls, and the collateral also loses USD value. As price drops, each further tick consumes more of the BTC margin of leveraged longs, so liquidation thresholds bunch up and forced selling begets more forced selling. On the up side, the BTC loss of leveraged shorts is concave and bounded. On USDT-margined linear contracts, PnL is linear in price and collateral is stable, so this convexity is absent. Down-move cascades should therefore run longer than up-move cascades on the inverse contract, by more than they do on the linear contract. A general down-vs-up asymmetry (leverage effect, panic) and any general venue or era difference are main effects; the contract-design channel lives only in the interaction.
COMPONENTS: Down-move direction of the triggering 5m jump
Inverse-collateral contract structure of BitMEX XBTUSD versus USDT-margined Binance perpetual

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BitMEX XBTUSD 5m closes for trigger jumps, run lengths and daily RV bins on the inverse contract
Binance BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 5m for trigger jumps, run lengths and daily RV bins on the linear contract

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate to high. It is a rare structural identification of a contract-design channel in path morphology using only ready data, and it adds a base mechanism (payoff convexity) that later composite claims can draw on.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The inverse-collateral convexity channel is rejected at 5m resolution if the interaction coefficient is at or below the 95th percentile of the day-sign-flip surrogate distribution, or if it is negative.
CARD.FUNCTION: Interaction characterization of path morphology in a 2x2 design, DIRECTION (down, up) x CONTRACT (BitMEX inverse in the pre-2020 sample, Binance linear in 2020-01..2024-12), estimated within daily-RV bins.
CARD.HORIZON: A run of at most 12 consecutive 5m bars (60 minutes) after each trigger bar
CARD.MECHANISM: Inverse-contract payoff convexity accelerates margin depletion of leveraged longs on falling prices. Down-move cascades should therefore be more contiguous on BitMEX XBTUSD than on the linear Binance perpetual, beyond the general direction asymmetry and the general contract difference.
CARD.NAME: Inverse-collateral convexity and down-move cascade run length
CARD.OBSERVABLE: RUN_LEN(J): the number of consecutive 5m bars immediately after trigger bar J whose return has the same sign as J and an absolute value of at least m trailing-30-day 5m return standard deviations. Trigger bars are 5m bars with |return| at or above the q-th percentile of trailing 30-day 5m absolute returns.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: The coefficient on the product of the down-direction and inverse-contract indicators in a regression of log(1+RUN_LEN) with daily-RV-bin fixed effects. This equals [inverse down minus inverse up] minus [linear down minus linear up] within matched RV bins.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Placebo times are drawn with the same weekday and UTC hour as each activation and lie at least 30 days away from any listed upgrade, with beta frozen in the same way. The null distribution of the event-mean RESID_H comes from repeatedly drawing as many placebo times as there are events. Under the null of no upgrade effect it reproduces the ETH residual statistic.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: A scheduled Ethereum mainnet upgrade concentrates protocol-failure risk at a pre-announced block: consensus splits, client bugs, or stalled finality. That risk is specific to ETH and absent for BTC. Some ETH holders, especially funds with mandates on operational risk, reduce ETH relative to BTC ahead of activation or carry offsetting relative positions. Makers in ETH also widen and lean their inventory. Once activation passes without failure, the risk is resolved and those relative positions are unwound, so ETH should outperform its BTC beta in the hours to days after activation. The calendar is set by core developers through public calls weeks ahead. It is exogenous to short-run ETH price action, which makes it a clean source of relative cross-asset variation.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: ETHUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 1h log returns
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 1h log returns
Fork activation block or epoch, its chain timestamp, and the timestamp of the first public announcement of the activation block for each mainnet upgrade

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Low to moderate given the small number of events. It adds an exogenous official-calendar base mechanism for ETH-specific risk, which the cross-asset library lacks.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The resolution-unwind mechanism is rejected if mean RESID_H across upgrades does not exceed the 95th percentile of the placebo distribution, or if fewer than half of the events show a positive RESID_H. With roughly seven events, a null whose placebo dispersion is wider than the hypothesized effect is reported as uninformative rather than confirmatory of no effect.
CARD.FUNCTION: Unconditional event characterization of the ETH idiosyncratic return, after removing BTC with a frozen pre-event beta, over a fixed window after each scheduled Ethereum mainnet upgrade activation. The candidate events to verify are Berlin 2021-04, London 2021-08, Arrow Glacier 2021-12, Gray Glacier 2022-06, Paris 2022-09, Shapella 2023-04 and Dencun 2024-03.
CARD.HORIZON: H in {24 hours, 168 hours} after each activation timestamp A
CARD.MECHANISM: Pre-announced hard-fork activation concentrates ETH-specific protocol risk at a known block. When activation passes without failure, holders who had reduced ETH relative to BTC unwind, leaving a positive ETH residual versus BTC after activation.
CARD.NAME: ETH residual return in the window after scheduled Ethereum network-upgrade activation
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Activation timestamp A of each scheduled Ethereum mainnet upgrade, defined as the chain timestamp of the fork block or epoch, admitted only when the activation point was publicly announced at least 7 days before A
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: RESID_H: the sum over 1h bars in (A, A+H] of [ETH log return minus beta_pre x BTC log return], with beta_pre fitted by OLS on 1h returns over (A-60d, A-7d], averaged across events

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: On each regime day, every name without perpetual cover is matched to a name with cover from the same trailing 30-day quote-volume decile, trailing 30-day volatility decile and log-price bucket, and the comparison is made within these cells. The null permutes the PERP_COVER label within those cells on each regime day, which preserves the cross-sectional distribution of the spread proxy and produces the full SPREAD_GAP statistic. The same gap on non-stress days is reported descriptively only, not as part of the claim.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Market makers quoting a Binance spot altcoin carry inventory risk. If the same base asset has a Binance USD-M perpetual, they can neutralize inventory instantly in the perpetual and keep quoting tight. If there is no perpetual, inventory must be worked off in spot, or covered only through a noisy BTC proxy. On days of large BTC moves, inventory turnover and inventory risk spike. Makers in names without perpetual cover face a binding risk limit and widen quotes or pull size, while makers in names with cover do not. The constraint is the availability of a same-asset derivative for inventory offset. Within the stress regime, the effective spread of names without cover should exceed that of matched names with cover.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Daily open, high, low, close and quote volume per USDT-quoted spot name, including delisted names and pinned listing dates, plus BTCUSDT daily returns for the regime flag
Announcement time and effective launch time of each USD-M perpetual per base asset, including later-delisted perpetuals
Per-symbol onboardDate and delivery or settlement dates for USD-M perpetual contracts

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It identifies derivative availability as a liquidity-supply mechanism in the cross-section, which no prior card isolated.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The perpetual-cover inventory channel is rejected in the stress regime if mean SPREAD_GAP over regime days is at or below the 95th percentile of the within-cell label-permutation null, or if it is negative.
CARD.FUNCTION: Regime fixed in advance: a BTC stress day is a UTC day d whose absolute BTCUSDT spot daily log return is at or above the trailing 365-day p-th percentile evaluated at the close of d. Within this regime only, compare the Abdi-Ranaldo spread proxy over days d+1..d+D between names without a Binance USD-M perpetual and matched names with one.
CARD.HORIZON: Days d+1 through d+D after each stress day d, with D in {2, 5}
CARD.MECHANISM: On BTC stress days, makers in spot names lacking a same-asset Binance perpetual cannot offset inventory and hit risk limits, so they widen effective spreads relative to matched names with perpetual cover.
CARD.NAME: Perpetual-cover spread gap on BTC stress days
CARD.OBSERVABLE: PERP_COVER_i(d): equal to 1 if a Binance USD-M perpetual on the same base asset had an effective launch at or before the close of day d and had not been delisted by then, and 0 otherwise
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: SPREAD_GAP: the mean over stress days d of [mean log Abdi-Ranaldo spread over days d+1..d+D for names without perpetual cover minus the same for matched names with cover]

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: The baseline is a logistic model of ENTRY_N on trailing RV_7d, RV_30d, the DVOL-minus-RV_30d gap and the year. The claim is the increment of TERM_SLOPE beyond that model. The first null permutes TERM_SLOPE in 30-day blocks relative to outcomes. The second is a HAR-RV surrogate path with an implied-volatility proxy built as a fixed smooth function of simulated past RV; it produces the term slope and the entry indicator jointly with no forward-looking information.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: BTC option dealers on Deribit are typically net short gamma in front-month options sold to directional and protection-seeking clients. When participants who expect a near-term volatility event (an unlock, a court ruling, a leverage build-up) demand short-dated protection, dealers must raise front-end implied volatility relative to longer tenors to ration their short-gamma capacity. An inverted front end therefore reveals concentrated, time-specific protection demand that realized history has not yet shown. If those participants are partly informed, the inversion should precede entry into a high realized-volatility regime. This holds beyond what the IV level relative to RV conveys, because the level mixes a broad risk premium with event timing, while the slope isolates timing.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Per-instrument mark implied volatility, strike, expiry and underlying index price at hourly snapshots, for interpolating 7-day, 14-day, 30-day and 60-day ATM IV
Hourly BTC DVOL index values for the baseline IV-minus-RV gap control
BTCUSDT perpetual 5m log returns for trailing RV controls and the RV_N outcome

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate to high. It separates event-timing information in the IV term structure from the IV level already covered, and informs whether paying for options history serves regime work.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The protection-demand timing mechanism is rejected for regime entry if the TERM_SLOPE coefficient beyond the baseline model lies within the central 95 percent of the block-permutation null, or if top-minus-bottom quintile entry frequency is not positive.
CARD.FUNCTION: Unconditional regime-transition characterization: test whether the front-end ATM implied-volatility term slope at a daily decision time relates to entry into the top realized-volatility tercile over the next N days, beyond realized-history and IV-level controls.
CARD.HORIZON: N in {3, 7} days after each daily decision time T at 00:00 UTC
CARD.MECHANISM: Inversion of the front-end implied-volatility term structure reveals concentrated short-dated protection demand absorbed by short-gamma dealers. That demand carries event-timing information and precedes entry into a high realized-volatility regime.
CARD.NAME: Front-end implied-volatility term inversion and entry into a high-RV regime
CARD.OBSERVABLE: TERM_SLOPE(T): ATM implied volatility at the short constant maturity minus ATM implied volatility at the longer constant maturity, interpolated from Deribit BTC option marks with snapshot times at or before T
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: ENTRY_N(T): equal to 1 if annualized RV from 5m returns over (T, T+N] lies in the top tercile of the trailing 365-day RV_N distribution evaluated at T, among days whose trailing RV_N at T is not in the top tercile. The contrast is the incremental TERM_SLOPE coefficient beyond the baseline logistic model.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Within the down-shock regime, top-tercile INFLOW_Z shocks are compared with bottom-tercile shocks matched on shock-magnitude decile and year. The null permutes INFLOW_Z labels among shocks within year x shock-magnitude strata, which produces the full RECOVERY_6H contrast. A placebo uses inflow measured over the same clock window one day earlier, (T-26h, T-24h], to test whether a generally high inflow level, rather than shock-window inflow, drives the result.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Many participants with spare capital keep stablecoin reserves in self-custody or off-exchange wallets for counterparty-risk reasons. When a sharp liquidation-driven drop opens a discount, those who want to absorb it must first move USDT on-chain to an exchange deposit address. This takes blocks plus exchange confirmation, minutes to tens of minutes. The transfer is visible on-chain before the capital is fully deployed in the order book. A large net inflow in the shock window marks discount-absorbing capital in transit. Shocks met by such inflow should recover more over the next hours than equally sized shocks without it, because that additional resting demand arrives once the forced flow is exhausted. The constraint is the custody-to-exchange transfer latency.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 1h returns for the regime flag, shock magnitude and RECOVERY_6H
USDT Transfer events with block timestamp, sender, recipient and amount on Ethereum
USDT TRC20 transfer events with block timestamp, sender, recipient and amount on Tron
Address-to-exchange attribution for deposit and hot wallets, with the date each attribution first became public

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It tests whether on-chain capital movement adds to shock recovery beyond the price and volume conditioning of D8, and clarifies whether exchange-label point-in-time work is worth funding.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The transit-capital recovery mechanism is rejected within down shocks in any of three cases: the top-minus-bottom tercile RECOVERY_6H contrast is at or below the 95th percentile of the within-strata permutation null; the contrast is negative; or the one-day-earlier placebo inflow produces a contrast of similar size.
CARD.FUNCTION: Regime fixed in advance: down-shock events, meaning 1h BTCUSDT perpetual bars whose log return is at or below the trailing 365-day s-th percentile of 1h returns, de-clustered by 12 hours. Within this regime only, compare the 6h signed recovery between shocks with high and low net USDT inflow to labelled exchange addresses during the shock window.
CARD.HORIZON: 6 hours after the close T of each down-shock 1h bar
CARD.MECHANISM: Within liquidation-driven down shocks, a net on-chain USDT inflow to exchange deposit addresses marks discount-absorbing capital in transit. Because of transfer latency it reaches the book once forced flow is exhausted, enlarging the 6h recovery.
CARD.NAME: On-chain stablecoin exchange inflow and recovery inside down-shock windows
CARD.OBSERVABLE: INFLOW_Z(T): the net USDT amount (ERC20 plus TRC20) moved into labelled exchange deposit and hot wallets with block timestamps in (T-w, T], excluding Tether treasury and intra-exchange transfers, minus the trailing 30-day same-hour median and divided by the trailing 30-day same-hour MAD
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: RECOVERY_6H: log(close at T+6h / close at T) for each down shock. The contrast is the top INFLOW_Z tercile minus the bottom tercile within shock-magnitude decile x year strata.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: The main-effect baseline regresses PERP_MOVE_SHARE_W on Relative near-touch depth of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot, on Relative quoted spread of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot, on the |Z_D| bucket, on hour-of-day and on the trailing 1h RV bucket. The claim is only the coefficient on the product of the two components, beyond both main effects. The null permutes LOG_SPREAD_RATIO within LOG_DEPTH_RATIO quintile x hour-of-day x month strata. This destroys the joint term while preserving both marginals and their coarse dependence, and it produces the full interaction statistic.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: When the Binance perpetual and OKX spot dislocate, cross-venue relative-value desks take liquidity on the venue where execution is cheaper, and makers on the other venue reprice passively toward the leader. Closure is split between the venues according to how cheaply each venue's resting liquidity is moved. Depth near the touch measures how far a given order walks the book. The quoted spread measures how stale and defensive the top of book already is. A venue that is only thin is walked but may refill fast; a venue that is only wide has defensive makers but deep resting size. A venue that is both thin and wide has makers who have already withdrawn and little size to absorb flow. Its price should carry a share of the closure larger than the separate depth and spread effects imply. This is a venue-structure claim about where adjustment happens, not about direction.
COMPONENTS: Relative near-touch depth of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot
Relative quoted spread of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Binance perpetual and OKX spot BTC aligned 5m closes for Z_D events and leg moves
BTCUSDT perpetual L2 book updates for depth within b bps of mid and quoted spread, averaged per 5m bar
OKX BTC-USDT spot L2 book updates for depth within b bps of mid and quoted spread, averaged per 5m bar
BTCUSDT perpetual best bid and ask price and size for a free cross-check of the perpetual spread

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate to high. It would give the first book-state account of where cross-venue adjustment happens and justify or retire paid L2 acquisition for venue-structure work.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The joint-thinness channel is rejected if the interaction coefficient lies within the central 95 percent of the stratified permutation null. It is also rejected if the coefficient has the sign opposite to the claim, meaning a perpetual that is jointly thin and wide absorbs less of the closure than the main effects imply.
CARD.FUNCTION: Interaction characterization of venue structure: at 5m dislocation events, regress the perpetual's share of absolute leg movement on relative depth, relative spread and their product, with dislocation-size, hour and RV controls.
CARD.HORIZON: W in {15 minutes, 60 minutes} after each 5m dislocation event close T
CARD.MECHANISM: A venue that is simultaneously thin in near-touch depth and wide in quoted spread has makers who have withdrawn. Its price absorbs a disproportionate share of cross-venue dislocation closure, beyond the separate depth and spread effects.
CARD.NAME: Depth-spread joint thinness and venue resolution of perp-spot dislocations
CARD.OBSERVABLE: For each 5m event with |Z_D| at least 2: LOG_DEPTH_RATIO(T) is log(perpetual depth within b bps of mid divided by OKX spot depth within b bps of mid), and LOG_SPREAD_RATIO(T) is log(perpetual quoted spread divided by OKX spot quoted spread), each time-averaged over the 5m bar ending at T
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: The coefficient on LOG_DEPTH_RATIO x LOG_SPREAD_RATIO in a regression of PERP_MOVE_SHARE_W. Here PERP_MOVE_SHARE_W equals |perpetual log move over (T, T+W]| divided by the sum of the absolute perpetual and spot log moves over the same window, which is defined for every event with any movement.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Placebo windows of the same length are placed at the other 23 UTC hour boundaries; for each, the window return is regressed on the 24h return ending just before the window. The 00:00 UTC slope must exceed the placebo-hour distribution, and must separately exceed the 08:00 and 16:00 UTC slopes, which share the Binance funding settlement but not the token rebalance. An out-of-mechanism placebo computes the same 00:00 UTC slope over 2022-12..2024-12, when the FTX tokens no longer existed. A day-block bootstrap of 1m returns produces the null distribution of the slope.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Cheng and Madhavan documented that leveraged ETFs with fixed daily leverage L must rebalance at each close by adding exposure in the direction of that day's return. The rebalance amount is proportional to L(L-1) x AUM x day return, and it produces end-of-day flows aligned with the day's move. FTX's BTC leveraged tokens (3x bull, 3x bear, and others) followed a documented daily rebalance near 00:02 UTC with the same algebra. Both bull and bear tokens add exposure in the direction of the day's move, because L(L-1) is positive for L = 3 and for L = -3. If their combined AUM was material relative to liquidity in that minute window, a BTC perpetual return aligned with the day's return should appear in the rebalance window. This reproduction tests whether a mechanically documented external flow mechanism leaves a footprint in Binance perpetual klines. It also checks the footprint against the exchange-funding clock, which coincides at 00:00 UTC.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes for DAY_RET, rebalance-window returns and placebo-hour windows
Documented daily rebalance timestamp, target leverage and intraday threshold rebalance rule for BTC leveraged tokens, from archived web captures

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It is a clean external benchmark with a built-in natural ending, which shows whether mechanically known flows of plausible size are detectable in kline data at all and calibrates later flow-footprint cards.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The leveraged-token rebalance footprint is rejected as detectable in Binance perpetual klines if the 00:00 UTC slope over 2020-01..2022-10 does not exceed the 95th percentile of the placebo-hour distribution, or does not exceed both funding-hour placebos. It is also rejected if the same slope is equally large over 2022-12..2024-12.
CARD.FUNCTION: Diagnostic reproduction of an externally documented flow mechanism, leveraged-ETF style daily rebalancing, on the BTC perpetual at the documented leveraged-token rebalance time. It is measured over the pre-specified sample 2020-01..2022-10, while the issuer operated, with a placebo sample 2022-12..2024-12.
CARD.HORIZON: A fixed window of L minutes starting at 23:57 UTC, with L in {10, 20}, around the documented 00:02 UTC rebalance on each day
CARD.MECHANISM: Fixed-leverage token issuers must add exposure in the direction of the day's return at their scheduled daily rebalance, by an amount proportional to L(L-1) x AUM x day return. This produces a rebalance-window return aligned with the day's return.
CARD.NAME: Leveraged-token daily rebalance footprint in the BTC perpetual (Cheng-Madhavan adaptation)
CARD.OBSERVABLE: DAY_RET(D): the log return of the BTCUSDT perpetual from the 00:00 UTC close of day D to the 23:57 UTC close of day D
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: The OLS slope of WIN_RET(D) on DAY_RET(D) over 2020-01..2022-10, where WIN_RET(D) is the perpetual log return over the L-minute window starting at 23:57 UTC of day D

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Within the Sunday regime, the anchoring contrast compares the STEP at the Chicago-anchored reopen hour with the STEP at the alternative UTC hour, the one that would be the reopen under the other US DST state. Pseudo-reopen steps are computed at every other full-hour boundary from Sunday 12:00 to 23:00 UTC. The null is a block bootstrap of whole-Sunday ABS_D paths across weeks within the same DST state. It preserves intraday shape, destroys any link between a week's DST state and its hour of step, and produces the full contrast statistic.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: CME bitcoin futures stop over the weekend and reopen on Globex at 17:00 Chicago time on Sunday, which is 23:00 UTC under US standard time and 22:00 UTC under US daylight time. Basis desks and institutions that reference CME then reprice the accumulated weekend gap between CME and crypto venues. To do so they offset CME exposure with spot-linked positions, because cash-and-carry books hold spot, and this sends concentrated flow to spot venues first. Binance perpetual participants respond with a lag, so the absolute perpetual-spot dislocation should rise transiently right after the reopen. If the reopen is the cause, the step must follow the Chicago clock and move one UTC hour with US DST. A fixed UTC hour or crypto-native Sunday-evening activity would not move.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Binance perpetual and OKX spot BTC aligned 5m closes for ABS_D on Sundays
US DST transition dates for mapping the Chicago reopen to a UTC hour
Weekly Sunday reopen time of CME bitcoin futures and the dates of holiday-modified reopens

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It adds a participant clock tied to a regulated venue's session, distinct from the DST and holiday anchors already studied, and needs only ready price data once the calendar is verified.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The CME-reopen clock mechanism is rejected in either of two cases. First, mean STEP at the Chicago-anchored reopen does not exceed the alternative-UTC-hour STEP beyond the 95th percentile of the block-bootstrap null. Second, the Chicago-anchored STEP is not positive and the pseudo-reopen hours show steps of equal size.
CARD.FUNCTION: Regime fixed in advance: Sunday windows containing the CME Globex weekly reopen of bitcoin futures (17:00 Chicago time), excluding holiday-modified reopens. Within this regime only, measure the change in mean absolute perpetual-spot dislocation from the hour before the reopen to the hour after it. Then test whether the change tracks the Chicago clock across US DST states rather than a fixed UTC hour.
CARD.HORIZON: M minutes on each side of the Sunday CME reopen, with M in {30, 60}
CARD.MECHANISM: At the CME Sunday reopen, basis desks reprice the weekend CME gap through spot-linked offsets, so spot venues move first and the absolute Binance perpetual versus OKX spot dislocation rises transiently. The step is anchored to the Chicago clock.
CARD.NAME: CME Globex Sunday reopen clock and Binance perpetual versus OKX spot dislocation
CARD.OBSERVABLE: ABS_D(t): |log(perpetual close / OKX spot close)| at aligned 5m closes on Sundays, minus its trailing median over a lookback ending at the start of the pre-reopen window
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: STEP: the mean ABS_D over (R, R+M] minus the mean ABS_D over (R-M, R], with R the Chicago-anchored reopen time. The anchoring contrast is the STEP at R minus the STEP at the alternative UTC hour, pooled across DST states.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Baseline: pooled linear-probability model (risk-difference scale, the scale relevant for abstention) of TAIL_DD with main effects for Name-level turnover attention spike and Market-wide BTC volatility state, plus controls for trailing 30-day quote-volume rank, trailing 28-day return rank, trailing 28-day own-volatility rank and listing-age bucket. A logistic version is reported alongside. The claim is only the increment of the joint term Name-level turnover attention spike x Market-wide BTC volatility state over those two main effects and controls. Null 1: within each week x liquidity-tercile stratum, permute the attention-spike label across names, preserving the number of spike names per stratum and each week's market-volatility state, then re-estimate the joint coefficient (1000 draws). Null 2: permute the market-volatility label across whole weeks within calendar year, keeping each week's cross-section intact. Inference is clustered by week because tail outcomes co-move across names.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Two actors are involved. First, attention-driven participants (mostly retail and short-horizon momentum traders) arrive in a name during a turnover spike; they hold small, low-conviction, often margin-funded positions with tight stop levels. Second, liquidity providers in small spot names quote against inventory that they offset with BTC or major pairs; when BTC volatility is high their offsetting instrument is itself volatile and their inventory risk becomes correlated across names, so they cut size first in the least liquid books. Each layer alone raises drawdown tails modestly: a new holder base is fragile, and high BTC volatility widens all books. Jointly, the fragile holder base tends to exit into books that makers have already thinned, so the drawdown tail should be super-additive. If the two layers act independently, the joint cell's tail frequency equals the additive prediction.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Daily OHLC and quote volume for all USDT-quoted spot names including delisted symbols, pinned listing and delisting dates, and BTCUSDT daily closes
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to daily closes, used as a cross-check of the market-volatility state

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It decides whether name-level abstention filters in this panel need a market-state interaction term or whether single-layer filters are sufficient. It also adds an attention-participation layer to the base-mechanism library, which no prior map signature covers.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The joint risk-difference term (joint-cell tail frequency minus the frequency implied by adding both main effects to the neither-cell frequency) lies inside the central 90% of either permutation null. Alternatively, it has the opposite sign in at least 3 of the 4 calendar years from 2021 to 2024 evaluated separately, or it reverses sign between the top and bottom liquidity terciles.
CARD.FUNCTION: Interaction characterization for conditional abstention. It estimates whether the cross-sectional frequency of severe subsequent drawdowns is elevated in the joint cell (attention spike AND high market-wide BTC volatility) beyond the additive main effects of each layer, controlling for liquidity, trailing return and trailing own volatility.
CARD.HORIZON: H = 7 or 14 calendar days from each Monday 00:00 UTC decision time T; decision times from 2021-01 to 2024-12, restricted to those whose outcome window closes on or before 2024-12-31.
CARD.MECHANISM: Abstention-relevant tail risk may arise when a name-level turnover attention spike coincides with a market-wide BTC volatility state. Attention-driven marginal holders and inventory-constrained liquidity providers in that name both withdraw when market-wide risk budgets tighten, so the subsequent drawdown tail should be larger than the sum of the two separate effects.
CARD.NAME: Attention-spike names under high market-wide volatility: joint drawdown-tail exposure in the Binance spot USDT panel
CARD.OBSERVABLE: At Monday 00:00 UTC decision time T, for each eligible name i: ATTN_i = quote volume summed over the 7 daily bars closed at or before T, divided by 7 times the median daily quote volume over the 30 daily bars ending 7 days before T. MKT_VOL = realized volatility of BTCUSDT daily log returns over the 7 daily bars closed at or before T, ranked within its trailing 365-day distribution at T.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: TAIL_DD_i(T) = 1 if the minimum over daily closes in (T, T+H] of log(close / close at T) is at or below log(1 - D), else 0. The continuous MAXDD_i(T) is reported as a secondary readout. A name delisted inside (T, T+H] contributes its final listed close and is flagged.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Null 1: the same ALIGNED_RET statistic at weekday decision hours when CME is open, matched on UTC hour-of-day, trailing 24h RV decile and |SYNTH_DEV| quantile bin; the claim requires the weekend mean to exceed the matched weekday mean. Null 2: a weekend-block bootstrap that resamples whole weekends with random sign assignment to SYNTH_DEV, which generates the same statistic under no directional content and respects within-weekend dependence. Baseline drift: the unconditional mean weekend perp return is subtracted after alignment, so a generic weekend drift cannot pass as forward-led drift.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: When CME bitcoin futures are closed, institutions that normally take or offset directional exposure on CME lose that venue. Some move that demand to Deribit options, which trade continuously. Customer demand for calls over puts, or the reverse, at a strike moves the parity-implied forward before options market makers have fully offset their delta in perpetual markets. Cross-venue relative-value traders then carry the price toward the options-implied level with a lag of minutes to hours. On weekdays the same information is absorbed through CME, so the lag should be shorter there. The regime is fixed by the exchange calendar, not by any outcome.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTC option best bid and ask by strike and expiry with exchange timestamps, plus Deribit index price at each quote
BTC option trade price, strike, expiry, timestamp and index price at trade, as a fallback for parity forwards built from trades
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes
US DST transition dates for mapping CME Central-time session hours to UTC
CME bitcoin futures weekly close and reopen times and holiday session schedules

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It would provide the first directional quantity in the library derived from options rather than klines. It tests whether price-discovery leadership migrates across instrument classes when a competing institutional venue is closed by calendar.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any of the following falsifies the card: the weekend mean ALIGNED_RET at H = 4 is at or below zero or inside the central 90% of the weekend-block bootstrap; the weekend mean does not exceed the matched weekday mean; or the weekend sign disagrees with the pooled sign in at least 3 of the 5 calendar years from 2020 to 2024.
CARD.FUNCTION: Conditional directional characterization. The regime is fixed in advance as the CME-closed weekend window: from the CME bitcoin futures Friday close (16:00 US Central time) to the Sunday reopen (17:00 US Central time), mapped to UTC with the US DST calendar and excluding CME holiday-extended closures unless they are in the pinned schedule. Within this regime only, the card estimates the mean sign-aligned Binance BTCUSDT perp return after decision hours where the options-implied synthetic forward deviates strongly from the perp price.
CARD.HORIZON: H in {1, 4, 12} hours; the window (T, T+H] must lie inside the same CME-closed weekend window; weekend decision hours from 2020-04 to 2024-12.
CARD.MECHANISM: While CME bitcoin futures are closed for the weekend, institutional directional demand that would normally go to CME is partly expressed through Deribit options. The put-call-parity synthetic forward on Deribit then moves before the Binance perpetual, and options market makers offsetting delta, together with cross-venue relative-value traders, pull the perpetual toward the options-implied forward over the following hours.
CARD.NAME: Options-implied synthetic forward deviation and Binance perpetual drift during CME-closed weekends
CARD.OBSERVABLE: SYNTH_DEV(T) = log(F_syn(T) / P_perp(T)) minus its trailing 7-day median at T. F_syn(T) = K + C_usd - P_usd, from the call and put mids at the strike nearest the Deribit index, for the nearest expiry meeting the expiry rule, sampled at the snapshot nearest to and at or before T. BTC-denominated premia are converted to USD with the Deribit index at quote time. P_perp(T) is the Binance BTCUSDT perp 1m close at T.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: ALIGNED_RET_H = sign(SYNTH_DEV(T)) x log(P_perp(T+H) / P_perp(T)) on the Binance BTCUSDT perpetual, averaged over weekend decision hours where |SYNTH_DEV(T)| is in the top quantile of its trailing 90-day distribution.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Matched controls: for each event, up to 5 non-event 5m decision times in the same calendar month with the same hour-of-week, the same trailing 24h RV decile and the same trailing 6h signed-return tercile, and with no deposit event within plus or minus H. Null: pseudo-events formed by reassigning event timestamps at random within month x hour-of-week strata. These pseudo-events produce DOWN_SHARE from the same price process, and the event-minus-control mean is recomputed 1000 times. Placebo: same-size BTC transfers to addresses not labeled as exchange deposit addresses.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Large holders (funds, miners, early holders) who move BTC onto an exchange are usually preparing to dispose of it there. Because a block of hundreds of BTC would move the book if executed at once, it is typically worked over hours by execution algorithms or OTC-to-exchange desks in slices. Each slice consumes bid depth and makers re-quote lower, which produces a staircase of small down legs with weak rebounds. Counterparties who watch the same chain data may lean against the flow in advance, so the net return over the window can stay near zero while the path shape is still asymmetric. That is why the outcome is path morphology rather than mean return.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Transactions with inputs, outputs, values, block height and block header timestamp
Exchange deposit address labels with first-labeled date and labeling source
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 5m closes

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds an on-chain supply-side base mechanism to the library, distinct from the stablecoin-demand events already mapped. It also tests whether on-chain intent shows up in path shape rather than in net return.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any of the following falsifies the card: the mean event-minus-control DOWN_SHARE at H = 6 lies inside the central 90% of the pseudo-event null; it is negative in at least 3 of the 5 calendar years from 2020 to 2024 evaluated separately; or the same-size placebo transfers to unlabeled addresses show an equal effect, which would point to a generic large-transaction or block-timing artifact.
CARD.FUNCTION: Atomic path-morphology characterization. It compares the downside-excursion share of the Binance BTCUSDT perp path after large exchange-deposit events with matched non-event windows.
CARD.HORIZON: H = 6 or 24 hours from the event decision time T; events from 2020-01 to 2024-12 whose windows close on or before 2024-12-31.
CARD.MECHANISM: A holder who moves a large BTC output (at least S BTC) into a labeled exchange deposit address is preparing to dispose of it on-venue. Such disposals are worked in slices over hours, which should produce a staircase-down path whose downside excursion dominates its upside excursion, even when the net window return is near zero.
CARD.NAME: Large-holder BTC exchange deposits and downside-dominant subsequent path shape
CARD.OBSERVABLE: DEP_EVENT: an on-chain BTC transaction whose outputs to point-in-time-labeled exchange deposit addresses sum to at least S BTC and are funded from a single input cluster, timestamped by its containing block.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: DOWN_SHARE_H = MAXDOWN / (MAXUP + MAXDOWN). MAXDOWN = -min over 5m closes in (T, T+H] of log(close / close at T), floored at 0, and MAXUP = max of the same quantity, floored at 0, both on the Binance BTCUSDT perp. Windows with MAXUP + MAXDOWN = 0 are kept with DOWN_SHARE = 0.5 to avoid selection on a defined ratio. The statistic is the mean event-minus-matched-control DOWN_SHARE.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Baseline model inside the regime: BETA_H regressed on trailing 7-day 5m ETH-on-BTC beta and the trailing 7-day ratio of ETH to BTC RV. The claim is the coefficient on REL_THIN(T) beyond that baseline. Null: permute REL_THIN across days within the same UTC hour-of-day and regime-membership stratum, moving whole days to preserve autocorrelation, and re-estimate the coefficient (1000 draws). Stale-depth placebo: REL_THIN measured 24 hours before T replaces REL_THIN(T), to separate an instantaneous depth state from a slow-moving pair characteristic.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: The actors are market makers and relative-value desks that quote ETH and BTC perps together and offset inventory across the pair. Common shocks usually arrive first through BTC. When ETH resting depth is unusually thin relative to BTC, the same cross-asset rebalancing flow moves ETH further, so ETH's beta rises. Inventory limits bind hardest when BTC volatility is high, because makers then face larger and more frequent cross-asset offsetting needs; that is why the regime is the high-volatility state. In calm regimes depth differences matter less because flows are small relative to resting size.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT perpetual bookDepth snapshots with cumulative notional by percentage band from mid and snapshot timestamps
Full L2 incremental book updates for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT perpetuals to reconstruct near-touch depth
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 5m returns
ETHUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 5m returns

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds an order-book determinant of cross-asset pass-through to the library. This separates liquidity-driven beta variation from the correlation-level structure already mapped under D4 and D10.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any of the following falsifies the card: the REL_THIN coefficient lies inside the central 90% of the day-block permutation null; the stale-depth placebo coefficient is as large as the contemporaneous one; or the coefficient changes sign between the halves of the regime sample split at 2023-07.
CARD.FUNCTION: Conditional relative-structure characterization. The regime is fixed in advance: hourly decision times T whose trailing 24h BTC realized volatility, from 5m returns closed at or before T, lies in the top part of its trailing 365-day distribution as set by REGIME_CUT. Within this regime only, the card estimates whether relative ETH-versus-BTC book thinness predicts the subsequent realized ETH-on-BTC beta beyond trailing beta.
CARD.HORIZON: H = 1 or 6 hours from hourly decision times inside the high-volatility regime; decision times from 2022-01 to 2024-12, subject to bookDepth coverage verification.
CARD.MECHANISM: Cross-asset market makers and relative-value desks that quote ETH and BTC perps and offset inventory across them transmit BTC shocks into ETH. When ETH near-touch depth is thin relative to BTC, each relative to its own trailing level, a BTC-originated shock meets less resting liquidity in ETH, so ETH's pass-through beta over the following hours should be higher. This inventory constraint binds in the high-volatility regime.
CARD.NAME: Relative ETH-versus-BTC book thinness and ETH pass-through beta in high-volatility hours
CARD.OBSERVABLE: REL_THIN(T) = log(DEPTH_BTC(T) / MED30_BTC(T)) - log(DEPTH_ETH(T) / MED30_ETH(T)). DEPTH is the summed bid plus ask notional within plus or minus B of mid in the Binance USD-M bookDepth snapshot at or before T, and MED30 is the trailing 30-day median of the same UTC hour-of-day snapshot. Positive values mean ETH is relatively thinner.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Coefficient on REL_THIN(T) in a regression, within the regime, of BETA_H(T) on trailing 7-day 5m beta, trailing ETH-to-BTC RV ratio and REL_THIN(T). BETA_H(T) is the OLS slope of ETHUSDT perp 5m log returns on BTCUSDT perp 5m log returns over (T, T+H].

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Two-sided bursts (ONE_SIDE at or below 0.3) matched on quote-volume percentile bin, absolute 1m return bin, UTC hour and calendar year. Null 1: permute the one-sided versus two-sided label within each matched stratum (1000 draws). Null 2: compute IMPACT_RATIO at random non-burst minutes with the same pre-window impact decile, to measure mechanical reversion of the ratio. Bursts with another burst inside the outcome window are excluded from both arms.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Market makers on the Binance BTC perpetual quote both sides under inventory limits. A taker burst that is overwhelmingly one-sided leaves the makers who filled it with a large net position. Until they offset it on other venues or wait for opposite flow, they quote smaller size and wider spreads, so each unit of subsequent volume moves price more. A burst of the same size that is two-sided nets out across makers and leaves aggregate inventory roughly flat, so resilience should be unaffected. Matching on volume and absolute return isolates the inventory channel from the pure activity channel.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT perpetual 1m OHLC, quote volume and taker-buy quote volume

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds a minute-scale maker-inventory resilience mechanism to the library. This separates inventory loading from activity level, which hourly impact persistence (D7) could not.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any of the following falsifies the card: the one-sided minus two-sided mean IMPACT_RATIO at W = 30 is at or below zero, or lies inside the central 90% of the label-permutation null; the difference is no larger than the reversion measured by Null 2; or the sign disagrees with the pooled sign in at least 3 of the 5 calendar years from 2020 to 2024.
CARD.FUNCTION: Atomic liquidity-state characterization. It compares the post-burst execution-impact ratio after one-sided 1m taker bursts with that after volume-matched two-sided bursts.
CARD.HORIZON: W = 15, 30 or 60 minutes from the close of the burst bar; bursts from 2020-01 to 2024-12.
CARD.MECHANISM: Liquidity providers who absorb a one-sided taker burst end the minute carrying inventory. Until that inventory is offset they quote less size, so impact per unit of volume should stay elevated for tens of minutes. A two-sided burst of equal volume leaves aggregate maker inventory roughly flat and should not depress resilience.
CARD.NAME: Inventory-loading one-sided bursts and minute-scale liquidity resilience on the BTC perpetual
CARD.OBSERVABLE: BURST(t): a 1m Binance BTCUSDT perp bar whose quote volume is at or above quantile q of the trailing 30-day per-minute quote-volume distribution at t. ONE_SIDE(t) = 2 x |taker-buy quote volume / quote volume - 0.5|. A burst is one-sided if ONE_SIDE is at or above theta and two-sided if ONE_SIDE is at or below 0.3.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: IMPACT_RATIO_W = log[(sum of |1m log returns| / sum of 1m quote volume) over (t, t+W]] - log[the same ratio over the 60 minutes ending at the start of bar t]. The statistic is the mean IMPACT_RATIO_W for one-sided bursts minus that for matched two-sided bursts.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Baseline: logistic hazard of TRANSITION_H on main effects of Perp premium over OKX spot elevated, Low trailing BTC realized volatility, Perp-led cross-venue lead-lag and Elevated perp participation, plus UTC-hour and calendar-quarter controls. The claim is the increment of the four-way joint-state indicator over those main effects; a secondary check also includes all pairwise products. Null: circularly shift the daily series of each component by independent random offsets within the sample (1000 draws). This destroys co-occurrence while preserving each component's marginal frequency and autocorrelation, and the joint-state transition frequency minus its additive prediction is recomputed.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Leveraged traders build positions in the perpetual while spot buyers do not confirm, which shows up as a perp premium over OKX spot, perp-led price discovery and rising perp participation. Low realized volatility keeps margin requirements and liquidation distances comfortable, so positions keep growing. The resulting state is fragile because liquidation thresholds are concentrated in one venue. A modest move forces margin calls there, and cross-venue relative-value traders transmit the forced flow to spot. Each component alone is a weak and common condition; the hypothesis is that only their co-occurrence marks fragile leverage.
COMPONENTS: Perp premium over OKX spot elevated

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Aligned 5m closes of the Binance BTCUSDT perpetual and OKX BTC spot
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes and quote volume for RV and participation state

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It tests whether volatility transitions are better described by a joint cross-venue leverage state than by compression alone. It is also the first composite in the library built only from cross-venue kline observables, without blocked OI or funding data.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The joint-state increment over main effects lies inside the central 90% of the circular-shift null. Alternatively, the joint state contains fewer than 15 non-overlapping episodes, in which case it is reported as untestable rather than positive, or the increment's sign differs from the pooled sign in at least 2 of the 3 calendar years 2022, 2023 and 2024.
CARD.FUNCTION: Composite regime-transition characterization. It estimates whether the joint state of a perp premium over spot, low realized volatility, perp-led lead-lag and elevated perp participation predicts low-to-high volatility transitions beyond each component taken separately.
CARD.HORIZON: H = 24 or 72 hours from hourly decision times T; decision times from 2022-04 to 2024-12 whose windows close on or before 2024-12-31.
CARD.MECHANISM: Volatility transitions may start from a fragile calm in which leveraged positioning concentrates in the perpetual without spot confirmation. In that state the perp trades at a premium to spot, leads price discovery and draws rising participation, while low realized volatility keeps margin requirements loose. A modest shock then forces concentrated perp liquidations that cross-venue traders spread to spot, producing a regime transition.
CARD.NAME: Leverage-led fragile calm: joint cross-venue state and low-to-high volatility transitions
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Four binary components at hourly decision time T. (1) PREM(T), the mean over the 24h ending at T of log(Binance perp 5m close / OKX spot 5m close), in the top quantile q of its trailing 90-day distribution. (2) Trailing BTC RV over lookback L from Binance perp 5m returns in the bottom tercile of its trailing 365-day distribution. (3) LL(T) = corr(perp r(t-1), spot r(t)) - corr(spot r(t-1), perp r(t)) over 5m returns in the 24h ending at T, positive and in the top tercile of its trailing 90 days. (4) Perp 24h quote volume at or above 1.5 times the median 24h quote volume over the trailing 30 days.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: TRANSITION_H(T) = 1 if the trailing-24h BTC realized volatility evaluated at any hourly close in (T, T+H] enters the top tercile of the 365-day distribution frozen at T. Eligibility is limited to decision hours whose RV at T is not already in the top tercile; this selection uses only information at T.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Matched comparison inside the regime: each down shock is matched to up shocks on the same |shock| quantile bin, trailing 24h RV decile, UTC hour and calendar quarter. Null 1: permute shock-sign labels within matched strata and recompute the down-minus-up recovery (1000 draws). Null 2: a stationary block bootstrap of the BitMEX 5m return series, which produces shocks and recoveries with no sign-specific forced-flow mechanism. Diagnostic only, not part of the claim: the same statistic on the linear USDT-margined Binance perp from 2020-01 to 2024-12.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: On BitMEX XBTUSD, leveraged long holders post BTC as collateral. When price falls, their position loses value and the USD value of their collateral falls too, so margin ratios collapse faster than in a linear contract and liquidations cascade convexly. Holders of the opposite position have collateral that gains USD value as price rises, which damps their liquidations. Liquidation flow is forced and carries no information, so the part of a move driven by liquidations tends to be recovered as liquidity providers and value-oriented participants step in. Down shocks therefore contain more forced flow and should be recovered more than up shocks of the same size.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BitMEX XBTUSD 5m OHLC closes
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m closes aggregated to 5m for the linear-margin diagnostic

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds a contract-design mechanism (collateral convexity) to the event-response library. The pre-2020 surface provides a regime that the Binance-era data cannot.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Within the BitMEX regime, the mean down-minus-up REC at H = 6 is at or below zero, or lies inside the central 90% of the sign-permutation null. As a separate test of attribution, the down-minus-up asymmetry on the linear Binance perp is equal to or larger than on BitMEX, which would point to generic downside overshoot rather than inverse-margin convexity.
CARD.FUNCTION: Conditional event-response characterization. The regime is fixed in advance: the inverse-margined BitMEX XBTUSD venue in the full pre-2020 5m sample pinned in the catalog, when BitMEX hosted a dominant share of BTC perpetual positioning. Within that regime, the card compares recovery after extreme down 5m shocks with recovery after extreme up 5m shocks.
CARD.HORIZON: H = 1 or 6 hours from the close of each shock bar, within the pre-2020 BitMEX XBTUSD 5m sample; the Binance diagnostic uses shock bars from 2020-01 to 2024-12.
CARD.MECHANISM: In the inverse-margined BitMEX contract, collateral is denominated in BTC, so a price fall erodes both position equity and collateral value and makes long liquidations convex. Price rises damp liquidations of the opposite position. Down shocks should therefore carry a larger non-informational forced-flow component, which is later recovered more than in up shocks.
CARD.NAME: Inverse-margin liquidation convexity and down-versus-up shock recovery on BitMEX XBTUSD
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Shock bars are 5m XBTUSD bars whose |log return| is at or above quantile q of the trailing 30-day 5m |return| distribution, with sign s = +1 for up and -1 for down. Shocks within H of a prior shock are excluded.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: REC_H = -s x log(close at T+H / close at T) / |shock log return|, where T is the shock bar close. The statistic is mean REC_H over down shocks minus mean REC_H over matched up shocks.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Placebo months: the same LOSER_TURN_GAP is computed at day D of each of the 11 non-December months of year Y, with formation over the trailing returns ending at that day and outcome over the rest of that month. The null is that December's gap ranks uniformly among the 12 monthly gaps of each year; pooled over 5 years, a rank-sum test is used. Controls: ABN_TURN is residualized cross-sectionally on trailing 30-day return rank, trailing volatility rank and liquidity rank before forming the gap, so generic loser-turnover patterns are removed.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Taxable holders on a calendar tax year, including US individuals and holders in many other jurisdictions, have an incentive to realize capital losses before 31 December. In equities the US wash-sale rule makes holders wait 30 days before re-establishing exposure, which creates net price pressure. For digital assets in tax years from 2020 to 2024 the rule did not apply, so holders could realize a loss and re-enter exposure within minutes. That predicts concentrated two-way turnover in the largest calendar-year losers during late December. The outcome is turnover because round trips without a waiting period should leave volume, not necessarily price, as the footprint.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Daily closes and quote volume for all USDT-quoted spot names including delisted symbols, with pinned listing dates
Pinned statutory text and IRS guidance on calendar tax-year end and wash-sale scope for digital assets

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds a cross-sectional mechanism anchored to an official calendar in which the identification comes from a statutory date, not from price. It also tests a regulatory asymmetry between crypto and equities.
CARD.FALSIFIER: December's LOSER_TURN_GAP is not among the top 3 of the 12 monthly gaps in at least 3 of the 5 years from 2020 to 2024, or the pooled rank-sum lies inside the central 90% of the uniform-rank null. It is also falsified if the December gap disappears once the formation return is replaced by the trailing 30-day return, which would indicate turnover driven by short-term losses rather than tax-year anchoring.
CARD.FUNCTION: Atomic cross-sectional characterization anchored to the official calendar tax-year end. It measures whether the largest calendar-year losers in the Binance spot USDT cross-section show abnormal late-December turnover relative to winners, compared with placebo month-ends.
CARD.HORIZON: Outcome window from day D+1 to 31 December of each year from 2020 to 2024; formation from the first daily bar of that calendar year to day D of December.
CARD.MECHANISM: Taxable holders on a calendar tax year realize losses before 31 December. Because the US wash-sale rule did not cover digital assets in tax years from 2020 to 2024, they can re-enter exposure immediately. The mechanism therefore predicts abnormal two-way turnover concentrated in the largest calendar-year losers during late December.
CARD.NAME: Tax-year-end loss realization without a wash-sale constraint: late-December turnover of calendar-year losers
CARD.OBSERVABLE: CY_LOSS_RANK_i = cross-sectional rank of R_i = log(close at day D of December / first daily close of the same calendar year), for names listed throughout that calendar year.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: LOSER_TURN_GAP(Y) = mean residualized ABN_TURN over the bottom calendar-year-return group minus the mean over the top group in December of year Y, ranked against the 11 placebo-month gaps of year Y. ABN_TURN_i = log(mean daily quote volume over day D+1 to 31 December / mean daily quote volume over the 60 days ending at day D).

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Baseline: a weekly Fama-MacBeth regression with control ranks only (trailing 30-day quote volume as a size proxy, trailing 28-day return and trailing 28-day volatility). The MAX coefficient is measured in a model that includes these controls. Null: a weekly sign-flip Monte Carlo on the MAX slopes (as in D13), with non-overlapping holding windows or Newey-West correction for H = 28. Placebo: the rank of MIN, the minimum daily return over the same window, replaces MAX. The unconditional all-weeks slope is reported as a diagnostic and is not the claim.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: The external benchmark is the MAX effect documented in equities by Bali, Cakici and Whitelaw: investors who prefer lottery-like payoffs overpay for assets that recently delivered extreme single-day gains, and those assets then underperform. In crypto the marginal holders of small names are largely retail participants with strong lottery preferences, and their inflows are largest in risk-on phases when BTC has been rising. The overpricing should therefore be largest, and its correction most measurable, inside the risk-on regime. The regime is fixed by BTC's trailing return at the decision time, which is public at T.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Daily closes and quote volume for all USDT-quoted spot names including delisted symbols, pinned listings, and BTCUSDT daily closes for the regime

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It provides a clean regime-conditioned reproduction of a well-known external mechanism. This calibrates whether behavioral cross-sectional benchmarks transfer to crypto and whether they depend on market phase.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any of the following falsifies the card: the mean risk-on MAX slope is at or above zero, or lies inside the central 90% of the sign-flip null; the MAX slope disappears once trailing volatility rank is included, so MAX is only a volatility proxy; the MIN placebo shows a slope of equal size and sign; or the risk-on slope has a sign different from the pooled sign in at least 3 of the 5 calendar years from 2020 to 2024.
CARD.FUNCTION: Conditional reproduction of an external benchmark. The regime is fixed in advance: Monday 00:00 UTC decision times T at which BTCUSDT's 28-day log return over daily closes at or before T is positive. Within these weeks only, the card estimates the cross-sectional association between a name's maximum recent daily return and its subsequent relative return, controlling for size proxy, trailing return and trailing volatility.
CARD.HORIZON: H = 7 or 28 days from weekly decision times T; decision times from 2020-03 to 2024-12 whose outcome windows close on or before 2024-12-31.
CARD.MECHANISM: This reproduces the externally documented MAX effect: participants with lottery preferences overpay for names whose recent maximum daily return is extreme, and those names then underperform. Here it is tested only inside a risk-on regime, when retail lottery demand in small crypto names is expected to be largest.
CARD.NAME: Lottery-demand MAX effect in the Binance spot USDT cross-section inside a risk-on regime
CARD.OBSERVABLE: MAX_i(T) = maximum daily log return of name i over the 28 daily bars closed at or before T; the variant is the mean of the top 3 daily returns.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Mean over risk-on weeks of the weekly Fama-MacBeth slope of relative log return over (T, T+H] on the cross-sectional rank of MAX_i(T), with control ranks included. The relative return is the name's return minus the equal-weight eligible-universe return. The external benchmark predicts a negative sign.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Pseudo-transition null: the same SHIFT statistic computed at pseudo-Sundays, meaning non-transition Sundays at least 3 weeks from any US or EU DST transition, with identical 1-week before and after windows and the same weekday composition. This null produces the observable from the same activity process with no clock change. Reference comparison, not the claim: the same statistic on the Binance BTCUSDT perp hourly quote-volume profile over identical windows.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Deribit BTC options expire every day at 08:00 UTC throughout the year, which gives a contractual UTC anchor. A large part of Deribit options activity comes from European-based market makers and institutional desks whose working day is set by local clocks, which shift by one UTC hour at EU DST transitions. If participants' working hours dominate, the morning ramp of option activity moves one UTC hour at each EU transition. If the expiry and associated rolling dominate, the profile stays fixed in UTC. Windows are chosen so that the US clock does not change inside them, which isolates the EU clock.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTC option trade timestamps, strike and expiry for hourly trade counts
US and EU DST transition dates
BTCUSDT perpetual hourly quote volume for the reference profile
Deribit option expiry time policy records

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds an options-venue participant-clock measurement to the library. It distinguishes contractual from participant anchoring in a venue where the two clocks can be separated, which complements the perp-based DST work.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Mean SHIFT_EU over the 10 transitions lies inside the central 90% of the pseudo-Sunday null, which indicates anchoring to the UTC expiry clock or a global mix. It is also falsified if SHIFT_EU is not distinguishable from the Binance perp reference shift computed on the same windows, which would mean there is no options-specific participant clock.
CARD.FUNCTION: Atomic participant-clock characterization. It estimates the displacement, in UTC hours, of the Deribit BTC option trade-count intraday profile across EU DST transitions, using windows in which the US clock is unchanged.
CARD.HORIZON: One week before and one week after each EU DST transition from 2020-03 to 2024-11, totalling 10 transitions.
CARD.MECHANISM: Deribit options expire at 08:00 UTC year-round, a contractual UTC anchor, while many of its market makers and desks keep European working hours that shift by one UTC hour at EU DST transitions. If participant clocks dominate, the intraday option-activity profile should move with the EU clock; if the expiry clock dominates, it should stay fixed in UTC.
CARD.NAME: Which clock governs Deribit BTC option activity: fixed-UTC expiry versus European working hours
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Hourly count of Deribit BTC option trades across all strikes and expiries, normalized to a daily share profile over UTC hours and averaged over the 7 days of each window.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: SHIFT_EU = the UTC-hour displacement, on a 0.25-hour grid from -1.5 to 1.5 with interpolated profiles, that best aligns the after-window profile with the before-window profile. It is signed so that +1 means a full move with the European clock and pooled as a mean over transitions.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Null 1: pseudo-credit depths K' in 1..12, excluding the true K, are applied to the same events and give a distribution of mean STEP. The true K should rank at the top if the credit rule clocks disposal. Null 2: equal-size transfers to unlabelled non-exchange addresses, with the true K applied and matched on UTC hour, weekday and year. Null 3: block arrival times are redrawn from an exponential with the same rate while the kline series is kept. This generates the STEP observable when there is no credit-clock link.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: The exchange confirmation policy is a rule-based delay that splits one event into two moments. The first is when the transfer becomes visible on-chain at the inclusion block, which every observer can see. The second is when the depositor can act, at the credit block. Reactions by observers to the information should load on inclusion. Mechanical disposal by the depositor should load on credit. Block arrival is close to a Poisson process, so the inclusion-to-credit gap varies randomly from event to event. That gives within-event identification: the taker-sell share should step up at the credit time, and the clock position of the credit time is random relative to hour-of-day effects. Disposal on Binance spot reaches the USD-M perpetual through cross-market intermediaries. The perp taker-sell share is therefore used as the measured footprint.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Block height, header timestamp, median-time-past and transaction outputs with values and addresses
As-of-dated label of Binance BTC deposit address clusters
Required BTC confirmation count for deposit credit by effective date
BTCUSDT perpetual 1m quote volume and taker-buy quote volume

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It separates the mechanical channel from the informational channel in on-chain exchange-flow metrics. These metrics are widely cited but rarely identified. Either outcome constrains how on-chain flow observables should be timed in later cards.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any one of the following falsifies the claim: (1) mean STEP for exchange inflows does not exceed the non-exchange control; (2) the true K does not rank above the median of the pseudo depths, in the pooled or in the per-year estimates; (3) the step appears equally at inclusion time, which would point to observer reaction rather than depositor disposal.
CARD.FUNCTION: Event-time characterization of whether disposal pressure is clocked by the exchange credit rule. Identification comes from the random gap between inclusion and credit.
CARD.HORIZON: Minutes per event: the window (I_e, C_e+W] with W of 15 or 60 minutes
CARD.MECHANISM: Holders who move BTC on-chain to a Binance deposit address in order to dispose of it cannot place spot orders until the exchange credits the deposit at a fixed confirmation depth K. If such inflows are motivated by disposal, aggressor selling pressure should be timed to the credit-eligible block rather than to the first-inclusion block. The reason is that the confirmation rule is a hard constraint on when the coins become usable.
CARD.NAME: Deposit credit-latency footprint of large on-chain BTC inflows to exchange addresses
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Events are single transaction outputs of at least MIN_BTC to an address labelled as a Binance deposit cluster as of the inclusion block. For each event e, I_e is the inclusion-block arrival time. C_e is the arrival time of the block at depth K_e under the confirmation policy in force at I_e. STEP_e is the taker-sell share of BTCUSDT perpetual 1m quote volume in (C_e, C_e+W] minus the same share in (I_e, C_e].
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Mean STEP_e over events, and the rank of the true confirmation depth K among pseudo depths 1..12 applied to the same events

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Baseline: matched out-of-regime sweeps within year x UTC hour x sweep-size x RV strata. Null 1: the CME_CLOSED label is permuted within those strata. Null 2: pseudo-closures of equal length placed Tuesday to Wednesday, which tests whether any 45-hour block produces the same ratio.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Replenishing depth is a supply decision by liquidity providers who face inventory limits. After a maker absorbs a sweep, the cost of re-posting is the cost of carrying unhedged inventory. That cost rises when the cheapest external hedge venue is shut. The weekly CME closure is scheduled and exogenous to crypto order flow, so the regime is fixed in advance. Inside it, the card measures the depth recovery process. In a frictionless maker model that process should not depend on the calendar.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT notional depth by percentage band from mid, per snapshot timestamp
1m OHLC, quote volume and taker-buy quote volume for sweep identification
Scheduled weekly and holiday closure intervals of CME bitcoin futures

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: It adds a base mechanism, maker replenishment speed, under an exogenous regime. This is a prerequisite for later composite claims about weekend execution cost.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Any one of the following falsifies the claim: (1) the in-regime half-life ratio lies inside the permutation null; (2) the effect disappears after normalizing depth by the regime's own baseline depth level; (3) the pseudo-closures produce equal ratios.
CARD.FUNCTION: Pre-stated regime CME_CLOSED covers Saturday 00:00 UTC to Sunday 21:00 UTC, plus full-day CME holiday closures on weekdays. Inside the regime, estimate the half-life of swept-side depth recovery after taker sweeps. Compare it with sweeps outside the regime, matched on sweep size, UTC hour and trailing RV bucket.
CARD.HORIZON: 0 to 120 minutes after each sweep minute
CARD.MECHANISM: Market makers on the Binance USD-M BTCUSDT book absorb a taker sweep into inventory and normally offload part of that risk on CME bitcoin futures or other hedge venues. When CME is closed, the hedge leg is unavailable and inventory limits bind sooner. Makers then re-post depth on the swept side more slowly. So within the closure regime, the half-life of depth replenishment after a sweep should be longer.
CARD.NAME: Weekend hedge-venue closure and maker depth replenishment after taker sweeps
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Swept-side notional depth within DEPTH_BAND_PCT of mid, taken from Binance USD-M bookDepth snapshots before and after each sweep minute. A sweep minute is identified from 1m klines: absolute 1m return beyond SWEEP_SIGMA times trailing-30d sigma, with the taker share on the sweep side above 0.7.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Log ratio of median HALF_LIFE inside CME_CLOSED to median HALF_LIFE of matched sweeps outside it. HALF_LIFE is the number of minutes until swept-side depth regains RECOVERY_FRACTION of the loss from pre-sweep level to trough. It is right-censored at 120 minutes and the median is estimated by Kaplan-Meier.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Baseline regression of RV_DECAY on separate indicators for each component: One-sided taker burst: 15m taker-buy share of quote volume outside the frozen trailing-90d percentile band; Trade fragmentation: 15m trade count per unit quote volume above the trailing-30d 95th percentile; Cross-asset synchrony: ETH 15m return of the same sign as the BTC shock and beyond 3 trailing-30d ETH sigma; Intrabar overshoot: the 15m extreme in the shock direction exceeds the 15m close by at least 40 percent of the 15m high-low range. Controls are log shock size, pre-shock RV level, hour-of-week and year. The claim is the coefficient on the all-four joint indicator over these main effects. Null: the joint label is permuted within year x shock-size strata, keeping the counts of each component fixed.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Volatility after a shock reflects how long the forcing persists. Discretionary information arrivals prompt repeated revisions by many participants. Liquidation flow is a finite stock that ends when margin-deficient positions are closed. Each footprint alone is ambiguous. One-sided taker flow also occurs with news. High fill counts per notional also occur with retail bursts. Cross-asset synchrony also comes from macro news. Intrabar overshoot also comes from thin books. The conjunction is the state in which forced, price-insensitive flow is most plausible, and the claim concerns that state alone.
